documents.content:
3.5 Reimbursable expenses shall include:
(a) travel, accommodation, and subsistence costs for Helios personnel incurred in connection with the Services, at rates set out in Schedule B, provided that such costs are pre-approved in writing by the Client where they exceed the thresholds set out in Schedule B;
(b) costs of third-party specialised testing or inspection services, where such services are required by law, grid code, or the manufacturer's recommendations and are not otherwise included in the Fees;
(c) customs duties, import levies, and clearing charges on spare parts and consumables imported for the Facilities, where such parts are not available locally; and
(d) any other expenses expressly agreed in writing by the parties.

3.6 Helios shall maintain accurate records of all reimbursable expenses and shall provide supporting documentation with each invoice. The Client may, on reasonable notice and during normal business hours, audit such records for a period of twelve (12) months following the submission of the relevant invoice.

3.7 Late payment interest shall accrue on any overdue amount at the rate of the Central Bank of Nigeria's Monetary Policy Rate plus two (2) percentage points, calculated on a daily basis from the due date until the date of full payment.

3.8 Without prejudice to any other remedy available to Helios, if the Client fails to pay any undisputed amount when due and such failure continues for thirty (30) days after written notice, Helios may suspend the Services until payment is received. Helios shall give the Client at least seven (7) days' prior written notice of any intended suspension. The suspension shall not affect the Client's obligation to pay the Fees, and the Contract Term shall not be extended as a result of any such suspension.

3.9 The Client shall not be entitled to withhold or set off any amount payable to Helios against any claim the Client may have against Helios, unless the claim has been finally determined by a court of competent jurisdiction or by arbitration in accordance with Article 17, or the Client has obtained the prior written consent of Helios.

4. TERM AND TERMINATION

4.1 This Contract shall commence on the Commencement Date and shall continue for a period of twenty-four (24) months (the "Initial Term"), unless terminated earlier in accordance with this Article 4. Maintenance Contract 2023-001 contract_term_months 24 months. Record status: current.

4.2 The Client may terminate this Contract for convenience at any time after the first twelve (12) months of the Initial Term, by giving Helios at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice. In the event of such termination, the Client shall pay Helios:
(a) all Fees and reimbursable expenses accrued up to the effective date of termination;
(b) a termination fee equal to ten percent (10%) of the Fees that would have been payable for the remainder of the Initial Term; and
(c) all reasonable costs incurred by Helios in demobilising its personnel and equipment.

4.3 Either party may terminate this Contract with immediate effect by written notice if:
(a) the other party commits a material breach of this Contract and fails to remedy such breach within thirty (30) days of receiving written notice specifying the breach;
(b) the other party becomes insolvent, is unable to pay its debts as they fall due, or has a receiver, administrator, or liquidator appointed over all or any part of its assets;
(c) the other party ceases or threatens to cease to carry on its business; or
(d) the Facilities are destroyed or rendered permanently inoperable, provided that the party seeking termination shall first use reasonable endeavours to agree a variation of this Contract to address the circumstances.

4.4 Upon termination for any reason:
(a) Helios shall deliver to the Client all documents, data, and materials belonging to the Client, and shall return or dispose of any Client-supplied equipment in accordance with the Client's instructions;
(b) the Client shall pay all amounts due and payable to Helios within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination;
(c) Helios shall provide a final report summarising the Services performed and the condition of the Facilities; and
(d) the provisions of Articles 9 (Confidentiality), 11 (Limitation of Liability), 13 (Insurance), 16 (Dispute Resolution), and 17 (Governing Law) shall survive termination.

4.5 Any termination of this Contract shall not affect any rights or obligations that have accrued prior to the effective date of termination.

5. RESPONSE TIMES AND SERVICE LEVELS

6.4 Without prejudice to any other right or remedy available to Helios, if the Client fails to pay any amount due under this Contract on its due date, Helios shall be entitled to:
(a) charge interest on the overdue amount at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, calculated on a daily basis from the due date until the date of actual payment, both inclusive; and
(b) suspend the provision of the Services (or any part thereof) upon giving the Client not less than seven (7) days' prior written notice of its intention to do so, provided that Helios shall restore the provision of the Services promptly upon receipt of the overdue amount and any accrued interest.

6.6 Helios shall submit to the Client, together with each quarterly invoice, a statement setting out any reimbursable expenses incurred during the relevant quarter and the supporting documentation for such expenses. The Client shall have thirty (30) days from receipt of such statement to notify Helios in writing of any disputed items. Any items not disputed within such period shall be deemed accepted.

6.7 The Annual Service Fee shall be reviewed annually with effect from each anniversary of the Effective Date. Any adjustment shall be calculated by applying the percentage change in the Nigerian Consumer Price Index as published by the National Bureau of Statistics for the twelve (12) months preceding the review date, subject to a maximum increase of eight percent (8%) in any single Contract Year. Any such adjustment shall be notified to the Client in writing not less than sixty (60) days prior to the commencement of the relevant Contract Year and shall take effect automatically unless the Client objects in writing within fifteen (15) days of such notification.

6.8 The Annual Service Fee may also be varied by agreement of the parties in writing where there is a material change in the scope of the Services, including but not limited to:
(a) a change in the number or capacity of the Facilities;
(b) a change in applicable laws, regulations, or grid codes that materially increases the cost of performing the Services; or
(c) a change in the frequency or duration of scheduled maintenance required by the manufacturer's recommendations or by the Client.

6.9 Any variation to the Annual Service Fee under this Article 6 shall be recorded in a written amendment to this Contract signed by the authorised representatives of both parties.

6.10 The Client shall not be entitled to withhold or set off any amount due to Helios under this Contract, whether in respect of a disputed invoice or otherwise, except to the extent that the amount is finally determined to be due by a court of competent jurisdiction or by an arbitrator appointed in accordance with Article 16.

Maintenance Contract 2023-001 annual_service_fee_naira 250000000 NGN. Record status: current.

6.11 Helios shall maintain proper books of account and records relating to the Services and shall, upon reasonable notice, make such records available for inspection by the Client or its appointed auditors during normal business hours for the purpose of verifying the accuracy of any invoice or statement rendered under this Article 6.

**7. CLIENT OBLIGATIONS**

7.1 The Client shall provide Helios with safe and unhindered access to the Facilities at all reasonable times for the purpose of performing the Services, and shall ensure that Helios personnel are not obstructed or delayed in the performance of their duties.

7.2 The Client shall provide Helios, at no cost to Helios, with:
(a) access to water and electricity supplies at each Facility;
(b) a secure area for the storage of Helios's tools, equipment, and spare parts;
(c) suitable office accommodation and communication facilities at each Facility; and
(d) such information, documentation, and data as Helios may reasonably require to perform the Services, including but not limited to as-built drawings, equipment manuals, and operational records.

7.3 The Client shall ensure that the Facilities are operated in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications and with good industry practice, and shall promptly notify Helios of any abnormal operating conditions, faults, or damage to the Facilities of which it becomes aware.

7.4 The Client shall obtain and maintain all permits, licences, and consents required for the operation of the Facilities and for the performance of the Services, other than those which are the responsibility of Helios under Article 8.

Change Request Log
documents.content:
---

CR-2024-043
Date of submission: 2024-06-03
Status: Under review by the client's technical committee.
Description: Change of lubrication oil brand for the gearboxes of the wind turbine units at the Katsina hybrid site. Proposed brand: Shell Omala S4 GX 320 (ISO VG 320). Currently using Mobilgear 600 XP 320. Rationale: longer drain interval and better low-temperature performance for the site's night-time ambient conditions. Cost impact: nil — the proposed brand is quoted at the same unit price as the current brand under Helios's bulk purchasing agreement.
Remarks: The client's committee asked for a copy of the manufacturer's compatibility statement for the gearbox model (Winergy PEAB 6016). Submitted on 2024-06-07.

---

CR-2024-044
Date of submission: 2024-06-06
Status: Rejected by client on 2024-06-11.
Description: Request to increase the liquidated damages cap for late completion of the Benin City substation refurbishment from 10% of contract value to 15%. Rationale: the civil works contractor (third party) has delayed the cable trenching, pushing the scheduled completion date by three weeks. Helios sought to limit its own exposure while the delay was being adjudicated.
Remarks: The client rejected, stating that the original cap was a negotiated term and that Helios should pursue its remedy against the civil works contractor directly. No appeal filed.

---

Change Request CR-2024-047 submission_date 2024-06-12. Record status: current.

CR-2024-045
Date of submission: 2024-06-07
Status: Approved on 2024-06-10. Implementation window: 2024-07-01 to 2024-07-05.
Description: Addition of a weekly vibration analysis service for the two (2) main transformers at the Port Harcourt industrial site. Scope: on-site data collection using a handheld vibration meter, quarterly report with trend analysis, and immediate notification of any alarm-level readings. Cost impact: ₦420,000 per month, added to the fixed monthly fee.
Remarks: The client's maintenance supervisor requested that the service be performed on Thursdays only, to avoid conflict with the site's own weekly testing schedule. Helios confirmed availability. Updated service schedule sent to the client on 2024-06-11.

---

CR-2024-046
Date of submission: 2024-06-10
Status: Pending client decision — review meeting scheduled for 2024-06-18.
Description: Replacement of the SCADA communication module at the Kaduna North solar farm. The current module (model: SMA Data Manager M) has had intermittent communication losses since April, causing the remote monitoring centre to lose real-time data for up to 45 minutes at a time. Proposed scope: supply and install one (1) replacement module, reconfigure the network settings, and verify data flow for 72 consecutive hours. Cost impact: ₦2,150,000 (fixed, inclusive of commissioning).
Remarks: The client asked for a comparison of the proposed module with the manufacturer's latest model. Helios provided a one-page comparison on 2024-06-11. The client's technical lead indicated that the latest model may be preferred, but no formal instruction has been received.

---

CR-2024-047
Date of submission: 2024-06-12
Status: Under review by the client's engineering team. No decision deadline communicated.
Description: Proposed change to add drone inspections to the quarterly preventive maintenance scope at the Enugu East solar site. Scope: one (1) aerial thermal inspection of all PV modules and string combiner boxes per quarter, using a drone equipped with a thermal imaging camera. Deliverables: georeferenced thermal map, annotated report of anomalies (hot spots, diode failures, soiling patterns), and a priority list for corrective maintenance. Cost impact: ₦350,000 per quarter, added to the fixed fee.
Remarks: Helios internal note — the drone inspection will be performed by our certified pilot (S. Adeyemi, licence no. NCAA/DR/2023-118). The client's engineering team requested a sample report from a similar site before they proceed. A redacted sample from the Kano West site was sent on 2024-06-12. The client also asked whether the drone flights would require a permit from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority for each visit. Helios confirmed that the site is within a permitted corridor and that the pilot holds a current remote pilot licence; however, a one-time notification to the NCAA regional office will be filed before the first flight. This notification will be submitted by the Helios HSE department at no cost to the client.

**CR-2024-049**
Date of submission: 2024-06-14
Status: Client feedback pending.
Description: Proposed change to replace the existing fixed-tilt mounting brackets on the Ibadan South array (rows 4 to 9) with adjustable tilt brackets. Scope: supply and install 144 adjustable brackets, re-torque all module clamps, and re-test the array's electrical output after adjustment. The adjustment would allow seasonal tilt optimisation of 5 degrees.
Cost impact: ₦4,800,000 (fixed, inclusive of all labour, materials, and testing).
Remarks: The client's asset manager requested this change after reviewing the performance ratio for the Ibadan South site, which has been 2.1% below the P50 forecast since January. Helios internal engineering note: the proposed brackets are a standard production item and are in stock at the Lagos warehouse; lead time is 2 weeks. The client asked whether the tilt adjustment would affect the module warranty. Helios confirmed that the manufacturer's warranty allows up to 10 degrees of seasonal adjustment without voiding coverage, and a copy of the relevant warranty clause will be attached to the final submission.

Change Request CR-2024-047 proposed_scope add quarterly drone thermal inspections of all solar arrays. Record status: current.

**CR-2024-050**
Date of submission: 2024-06-17
Status: Approved by client on 2024-06-20. Work scheduled to commence 2024-07-01.
Description: Proposed change to add quarterly drone thermal inspections of all solar arrays at the Enugu East solar site. Scope: one (1) aerial thermal inspection of all PV modules and string combiner boxes per quarter, using a drone equipped with a thermal imaging camera. Deliverables: georeferenced thermal map, annotated report of anomalies (hot spots, diode failures, soiling patterns), and a priority list for corrective maintenance. Cost impact: ₦350,000 per quarter, added to the fixed fee.
Remarks: Helios internal note — the drone inspection will be performed by our certified pilot (S. Adeyemi, licence no. NCAA/DR/2023-118). The client's engineering team requested a sample report from a similar site before they proceed. A redacted sample from the Kano West site was sent on 2024-06-12. The client also asked whether the drone flights would require a permit from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority for each visit. Helios confirmed that the site is within a permitted corridor and that the pilot holds a current remote pilot licence; however, a one-time notification to the NCAA regional office will be filed before the first flight. This notification will be submitted by the Helios HSE department at no cost to the client. The client approved the change on 2024-06-20 after reviewing the Kano West sample and the NCAA confirmation. The first inspection is scheduled for the week of 2024-07-08; the HSE department will file the NCAA notification by 2024-07-02.

---

**CR-2024-051**
Date of submission: 2024-06-18
Status: Withdrawn by Helios on 2024-06-21.
Description: Proposed change to relocate the inverter enclosures at the Abeokuta West site from ground level to plinths 600 mm high, to reduce flood exposure during heavy rain. Scope: fabricate and install 3 concrete plinths, lift and re-secure 3 inverters, re-run all DC and AC cabling, and re-commission the affected strings.
Cost impact: ₦1,650,000 (fixed).
Remarks: Withdrawn after a site survey by Helios civil engineers on 2024-06-20 revealed that the existing cable trenches already pass through the proposed plinth area and would require re-routing at an additional cost of ₦720,000, bringing the total to ₦2,370,000. The client's project manager declined the revised cost and asked Helios to propose an alternative flood mitigation measure. Helios is evaluating the installation of a drainage channel and sandbag barriers at the enclosure base, which the site team estimates at ₦380,000. No revised CR has been raised yet; the client has asked for a written proposal by 2024-06-28.

Date of submission: 2024-06-20
Status: Rejected by client on 2024-06-27.
Description: Proposed change to extend the warranty period for the newly installed battery storage units at the Enugu East site from the standard 24 months to 36 months.
Cost impact: ₦850,000 (fixed), representing the additional premium charged by the battery manufacturer for the extended warranty.
Remarks: The client's procurement team rejected the change, stating that the extended warranty is not a priority for the current financial year and that the existing 24-month warranty is sufficient. They requested that Helios focus instead on the upcoming scheduled maintenance of the battery cooling systems. No further action is planned on this CR.

---

**CR-2024-047**
Date of submission: 2024-06-12
Status: Pending client approval.
Description: Proposed change to add drone inspections to the quarterly preventive maintenance scope at the Sokoto South site. Scope: conduct aerial thermal imaging of all solar panel arrays and the 11 kV overhead line, capture high-resolution visual imagery of the substation equipment, and provide a digital report with annotated findings within five working days of each inspection. The drone flights will be performed by our certified pilot (S. Adeyemi, licence no. NCAA/DR/2023-118).
Cost impact: ₦2,350,000 per inspection cycle (fixed), covering pilot time, drone equipment, data processing, and reporting. No additional cost for travel or accommodation, as the pilot is based in Sokoto.
Remarks: The client's engineering team has requested a sample report from a similar site before they proceed. A redacted sample from the Kano West site was sent on 2024-06-12. The client also asked whether the drone flights would require a permit from the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority for each visit. Helios confirmed that the site is within a permitted corridor and that the pilot holds a current remote pilot licence; however, a one-time notification to the NCAA regional office will be filed before the first flight. This notification will be submitted by the Helios HSE department at no cost to the client. The client has not yet responded to the sample report or the NCAA confirmation. The Helios contracts manager followed up with the client's project manager by email on 2024-06-24 and again on 2024-07-01; no reply has been received as of this log entry. If no response is received by 2024-07-15, the contracts manager will escalate the matter to the Helios operations director for a decision on whether to proceed with the change or withdraw it.

Change Request CR-2024-047 status pending client approval. Record status: current.

**CR-2024-054**
Date of submission: 2024-06-23
Status: Approved by client on 2024-06-28.
Description: Proposed change to install additional bird guards on the 33 kV busbar supports at the Kaduna Central site, following repeated tripping incidents caused by bird activity during the wet season. Scope: supply and install 14 bird guard units, replace any damaged insulators, and perform a thermographic scan of the busbar after installation.
Cost impact: ₦620,000 (fixed), including materials, installation, and the thermographic scan.
Remarks: The client approved the change without further clarification. The installation is scheduled for 2024-07-05, during a planned outage window coordinated with the local distribution company.

---

**CR-2024-055**
Date of submission: 2024-06-25
Status: Withdrawn by Helios on 2024-06-30.
Description: Proposed change to upgrade the SCADA system at the Lagos Island site to a newer software version, adding remote monitoring of inverter status and alarm notifications via SMS.
Cost impact: ₦2,100,000 (fixed), covering software licence, installation, and staff training.
Remarks: Withdrawn after the Helios IT department discovered that the new software version is not compatible with the existing communication gateway at the site. The gateway would need to be replaced at an additional cost of ₦1,400,000, bringing the total to ₦3,500,000. The client's operations manager was informed and requested that Helios investigate alternative SCADA solutions. A revised CR is expected once the IT department completes its compatibility assessment, tentatively by 2024-07-10.

**CR-2024-056**
Date of submission: 2024-06-26
Status: Under review by Helios technical team.
Description: Proposed change to replace the existing lightning arresters on the 132 kV incoming feeder at the Kano North substation. The current units have been in service since 2016 and failed their last routine surge test on 2024-06-12. Scope: supply and install six new surge arresters, including all connection hardware, and carry out a full insulation resistance test on the feeder after installation.
Cost impact: ₦3,450,000 (fixed), including materials, labour, and disposal of the old units.
Remarks: The technical team is verifying the surge arrester rating against the latest fault level study for the substation. A site visit was carried out on 2024-06-27 and the team confirmed that the existing mounting frames are in good condition and can be reused. The client has been notified that a decision is expected by 2024-07-08.

---

**CR-2024-057**
Date of submission: 2024-06-27
Status: Quotation requested from three vendors.
Description: Proposed change to extend the solar PV array at the Abuja Central workshop by adding 48 additional panels (total 19.2 kWp) to the existing 75 kWp system. The extension is intended to offset increased workshop load from new battery testing equipment installed in May 2024. Scope: supply and install panels, mounting rails, DC cabling, and one additional string inverter; connect to the existing AC distribution board.
Cost impact: ₦8,750,000 (fixed), based on preliminary vendor pricing. Final cost to be confirmed after quotations are received.
Remarks: The client's facility manager requested this change verbally on 2024-06-20, and the formal request was submitted after the site walkdown on 2024-06-26. The existing inverter has one spare MPPT input, but the technical team confirmed that the spare input cannot handle the additional string size. The additional inverter is therefore mandatory. Quotations were requested from three approved vendors on 2024-06-28, with a return date of 2024-07-05.

---

**CR-2024-058**
Date of submission: 2024-07-01
Status: Approved by Helios internal review on 2024-07-02; forwarded to client for approval.
Description: Proposed change to modify the maintenance schedule at the Port Harcourt Riverside site to align with the wet season. Specifically, the proposed change would move the quarterly preventive maintenance visit scheduled for August 2024 to September 2024, and add a one-off inspection of the stormwater drainage channels around the transformer compound. The inspection would be carried out after the first major rainfall event of the season.
Cost impact: No additional cost. The visit will be rescheduled within the same contract year, and the drainage inspection will be included in the same site visit.
Remarks: The client's site engineer had previously raised concerns about vegetation growth and standing water near the transformer plinths after heavy rains in June 2024. The Helios site team confirmed that the drainage channels are partially blocked and require clearing. The rescheduling does not affect the total number of preventive maintenance visits due under the contract. Client approval is expected by 2024-07-12.

---

---

**CR-2024-060**
Date of submission: 2024-07-04
Status: Under review by client.
Description: Proposed change to upgrade the lighting at the Ibadan West warehouse from fluorescent fittings to LED high-bay units. Scope: replace 22 fluorescent high-bay fittings with 18 LED units of equivalent lumen output, install new control gear, and rewire the lighting circuits to separate the warehouse area from the loading bay.
Cost impact: ₦1,980,000 (fixed), including materials, labour, and disposal of the old fittings.
Remarks: The change was proposed following an energy audit carried out by Helios on 2024-06-18, which identified the fluorescent fittings as a significant source of energy loss. The client's operations manager has requested a breakdown of the energy savings and a payback period calculation before approving the change. This information was provided by email on 2024-07-07. The client has also asked whether the LED units can be supplied with a five-year warranty; Helios has confirmed that the preferred manufacturer offers a five-year warranty on the LED modules, but not on the control gear. The client is reviewing this point.
